title: Heat pumps are not delivering expected cost savings - GreenBuildingAdvisor
summary: GBA forum thread: a Maine homeowner's mini-splits beside an oil boiler gave little saving at 30-cent power; experts point to price ratios and installation.

assertions.quote: electricity relatively expensive (.30/kw), I’ve opted to turn the heat pumps off and go back to oil.
The first year our utility costs (oil and electric) were about $200 less than pre installation. Last year they were actually about the same
that "being cheaper" part is entirely dependent on your relative costs for different input energy types
heat pumps don't always pay for themselves in Norther climates in areas served by natural gas, because natural gas tends to be pretty cheap
it will take more input energy for a heat pump to heat your home if it's extremely cold outside
If the refrigerant charge is not right, that can severely impact the operational efficiency of the heat pump
it wouldn't surprise me if a typical old-school boiler will outlast a typical modern heat pump.
